summary: Prebuilt darwin/arm64 binary opens WebSocket-driven PTY to ccfly-controlled host
details: The package ships a single 6.5 MB darwin/arm64 Mach-O executable at bin/ccfly-setup and no source. Strings in the binary show it is built from Go package github.com/ccfly/rescue/cmd/setup and links github.com/creack/pty and github.com/gorilla/websocket. It contains hardcoded WebSocket endpoints referencing ccflycc.hn and latest.ccfly (both ws:// and wss:// schemes) with /approve and /redeem paths, plus a Chinese status string translating to 'client installed and paired'. The combination of a WebSocket client bound to a hardcoded remote host and a PTY driver is a remote-shell agent: bytes received from the WebSocket are used to drive a local pseudo-terminal, giving the operator of the ccfly endpoint interactive code execution on the host running the binary. The package itself has no npm lifecycle scripts and no bin entry, so `npm install` does not auto-execute the binary; execution occurs when a companion/parent package invokes bin/ccfly-setup on darwin/arm64 (the standard optionalDependencies platform-shard pattern). No source, build instructions, or hash pinning are provided, so the payload cannot be independently verified.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
